calls.title: Jeremy / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed key enhancements to the app's user experience, focusing on setting a default project view to streamline user engagement and reduce confusion. Jeremy Dorn advocated for minimizing the all-projects view, suggesting that it should be reserved for admin roles. Kari Kay proposed a revamped homepage designed as a project-specific landing page, allowing users to easily access key metrics. The approval flow and permission systems will remain unchanged, with clarification planned to avoid complexity. Ongoing onboarding experiments were reviewed to improve user guidance, while a new product analytics explorer tool is being developed for easier metric exploration. The team also aims to clarify how metrics are shared across projects to enhance data governance and trust in metric accuracy.
calls.keywords: Projects, Approval Flows, Onboarding, Product Analytics, Sample Data Experiments, Explorer UI

calls.title: Jeremy / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed the status and prioritization of key projects, emphasizing the need for tight scope management to prevent delays and scope creep. Approval flows are currently blocked by team setup issues, with Adriel investigating technical details while Kari confirmed minimal additional design work is needed. The experiment creation flow is under review for simplification, with plans for an iterative launch approach. Delays in the holdout scheduling project were acknowledged, highlighting the importance of reevaluating low-impact projects. Design reviews are being streamlined to focus on functionality instead of minor details. Recruitment negotiations are addressing exclusivity clauses to ensure flexibility in sourcing candidates. Overall, the meeting reinforced the importance of clear prioritization and honest evaluations of project viability.
calls.keywords: approval flows, experiment creation, project prioritization, design review, holdout scheduling, recruiter contract
